record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control
record.original_question: Characterize, and ideally parameterize, the full set of feedback gains that stabilize a given linear system under the output-feedback structures discussed in the source. Such a parameterization should make it possible to optimize additional design criteria once stabilization is achieved.

evidence.quote: Beyond the question of existence, it is of interest to be able to characterize (and perhaps parameterize) the set of stabilizing feedback gains.
Such a parameterization would then be useful for selecting gains with desirable properties beyond stabilization.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite-dimensional linear time-invariant control system
  x'(t) = A x(t) + B u(t),  y(t) = C x(t),
where A ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, B ∈ ℝ^{n×m}, C ∈ ℝ^{p×n}, and a static output-feedback law u(t) = K y(t) with K ∈ ℝ^{m×p}. The closed-loop system matrix is A + B K C, and the feedback gain K is called stabilizing if every eigenvalue of A + B K C has strictly negative real part. Define the stabilizing set
  𝒮(A,B,C) = { K ∈ ℝ^{m×p} : A + B K C is Hurwitz }.

Problem: Give an explicit characterization, and ideally an explicit parameterization, of the set 𝒮(A,B,C) for general triples (A,B,C). That is, find a (preferably finite-dimensional) parameter space Θ and a map Φ: Θ → ℝ^{m×p} whose image equals 𝒮(A,B,C), and such that Φ is amenable to further optimization (so that, once stabilization is guaranteed, secondary design criteria such as performance, robustness, or minimal gain can be optimized over Θ).

Equivalently, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on a matrix K ∈ ℝ^{m×p} for K ∈ 𝒮(A,B,C), expressed in a form that exposes the geometric/algebraic structure of 𝒮(A,B,C) (e.g., its connected components, its closure, and free vs. dependent parameters).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing and parameterizing the set of stabilizing static output feedback gains is widely regarded as a long-standing open problem in linear systems and control. It is known to be NP-hard in general, and the feasible set is typically non-convex and can be disconnected. Partial results exist (LMI/Riccati-based sufficient conditions, dissipative-Hamiltonian parameterizations, H∞ state-feedback parameterizations, iterative LMI methods), but no general explicit parameterization of the full stabilizing set is known.

status_evidence.title: Static Output Feedback — A Survey
status_evidence.snippet: The static output feedback problem is widely studied and still unsolved, often cited among the difficult open problems in systems and control.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the SOF stabilization/parameterization problem remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Parameterization of All Stabilizing H∞ Static State-Feedback Gains
status_evidence.snippet: Simplified parameterization of all H∞ static state-feedback controllers via a Riccati equation and a free parameter matrix; necessary and sufficient conditions for existence of SOF gains.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial parameterization results in restricted settings.

status_evidence.title: Static Output Feedback Stabilization — A story of people and matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Survey presenting SOF stabilization as a fundamental open problem with NP-hard complexity.
status_evidence.claim: Supports open status of the general parameterization problem.
